title: personal-kpi-weekly-checkin-elena-brooks-2026-04-10
body:
Week: 2026-04-06 -> 2026-04-10
Owner: Elena Brooks (eng-serving-runtime)
Summary: Quick check-in on my personal KPIs and OKR progress. Focus this week on stability work for KV cache, improving tail latency, and prepping the canary rollout plan for the quantized model variant.

Progress highlights:
- KV cache hot-path fixes: merged PR, roll forward to staging. Latency p95 on staging improved from 210ms -> 170ms for 512-token runs. (measured on canary cluster)
- Canary rollout plan for quantized-8 model drafted and reviewed with Hunter. Plan includes traffic split (5% -> 20%), automatic rollback thresholds (error rate > 1% or p99 increase > 20%), and alerting playbook.
- Docs: Added runbook notes for cache eviction debugging to internal ops doc.

KPI / OKR status (quarterly OKR: Reduce inference unit-cost by 18% while keeping p99 latency +-5%)
- KPI 1: p99 tail latency for common workloads (goal: <= 300ms) -> current weighted p99 = 285ms (across hosted-canary). Progress: On track.
- KPI 2: unit cost per token (goal: -18% vs baseline) -> current delta: -9%. Need additional batching/caching to hit target.
- KPI 3: automated canary rollouts adoption (goal: 90% of deployments use rollout) -> current: 62%. Next step: template + onboarding doc.

Blockers / Risks:
- Observability: missing trace context for some short-lived requests; makes diagnosing tail spikes harder. Need SRE help to add tracing hooks into continuous batching layer.
- Capacity: Dedicated cluster constraints next week may delay the wider canary traffic increase. Coordinating with infra to reserve 2 nodes for 48h window.
- Quality: Quantized-8 shows occasional token-level degradation on a small prompt set (edges). Need a short evaluation harness run (200 prompts) before promoting beyond 20% traffic.

Next week priorities (top 3):
1) Run the 200-prompt eval harness for quantized-8 + analyze failure modes (owner: me). Deliverable: evaluation report and suggested mitigations.
2) Implement and test trace context propagation in batching path with SRE (owner: SRE + me). Deliverable: end-to-end trace for single-token tail spike reproducer.
3) Finalize canary runbook and create a 'canary quickstart' template for PMs/SEs (owner: Hunter + me). Deliverable: template and 1-hour office hours slot.

Action items (todo):
- [ ] Schedule eval harness run (slot: Mon AM)
- [ ] Book infra nodes for canary burst (target window Tue-Wed)
- [ ] Draft trace-propagation PR and pair with SRE next Tue
- [ ] Publish canary quickstart in team channel and Confluence

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding a small sampler on the high-latency tail to capture full request context for 30s when p99 > threshold. Could be toggled by route.
- If eval shows quality regression, experiment with selective dequantization for first 32 tokens as a mitigation (cheap but may help prefix-sensitive prompts).
- Cross-team: ask product for a prioritized list of prompt sets used by top 10 customers for more realistic evals.

Retro (what went well / what to improve):
- Went well: faster PR turnaround this sprint; stage metrics showed clear improvement after cache fix. Team coordination on rollout plan was smooth.
- Improve: need better pre-rollout eval automation; manual steps slow us down. Also we should have a contingency plan for infra availability earlier in the sprint.

Estimated effort next week: 3 days engineering (me + SRE pairing), 1 day docs/onboarding, 1 day evaluation/analysis.

If blocked, escalate to Hunter and CC infra leads.

End of check-in.
summary: Weekly personal KPI check-in: KV cache fixes merged, staging p95 improved, canary rollout plan drafted. KPIs: p99 285ms (on track), unit-cost -9% (need more work), rollout adoption 62%. Next week: eval harness, trace propagation, canary quickstart.
